findings.reason: the node runs to SPEC `exact`, so a worker cannot implement or fail this case and must either invent a reader or stop on a blocker; the case has to be replaced with the actual readers (`run_record`, `run_store`, `ledger`) that case 2 already names.
findings.text: §6's third done-when case ("the readers in `recovery_watch` and `dispatch_peer` read an old row the same as a new one") names a reading that does not exist: `follow_on_paths` occurs in exactly four production files at HEAD — `reckon/ledger.py:650`, `reckon/run_record.py:397/605/611/612`, `reckon/run_store.py:45` and `reckon/crew/promotion.py:1267/1268/1442` — and in neither `reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py` nor `reckon/crew/dispatch_peer.py`, so no ledger row is read there and no old-row behaviour can be asserted

findings.reason: the list is the §6 worker's census, and either it tries a field rename §6 forbids or it skips those files and leaves the retired word in a manifest template and a snapshot assertion that no section's done-when covers.
findings.text: §6's Why lists `reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_peer.py` and `scripts/check_snapshot_assertions.py` among "the key's users at `origin/main` that day", but those three hold only the manifest field `follow_ons` (`recovery_watch.py:201` writes `follow_ons: none` into a derived manifest, `dispatch_peer.py:407` into a NEEDS-HELP report, `check_snapshot_assertions.py:147` into the expected snapshot field set), not the ledger key; the reason the mismatch matters is that §6 scopes its change to "every file listed above" while stating "the rename changes no other field", and §3's write paths (`reckon/crew/prompts.py`, `reckon/crew/reports.py`, `reckon/crew/promotion.py`, the two comment-only sites) omit all three, so the retired field name in those emitted templates is owned by no section

findings.reason: with no caller named, removing the function stops no code path and §3's first case ("promotes with no plan followup written", plan.html:62) and its negative control ("restore the followup conversion, and the first case finds a followup written") have no arm that can fail, so the node's whole measure rests on a suite that passes on the unmodified store.
findings.text: §3 states "Promotion no longer turns entries into plan followups: `reckon/crew/reports.py`'s conversion (near line 2797) is removed", but that conversion runs on no production path: `followup_ops_from_manifest` occurs in the tree only at its definition (`reckon/crew/reports.py:2790`), in the public-surface export list (`reckon/crew.py:193`) and in two skill references (`skills/reckon-build/references/worker-protocol.md:138`, `skills/reckon-build/references/coordinator-reference.md:1025`), and `reckon/crew/promotion.py` holds no followup-building code at all, so the caller is the coordinator's writeback and not promotion

findings.reason: the followup is what a coordinator reads to sequence the build, and it omits the one dependency §3 now waits on while naming a satisfied one, so the ordering text has to be brought in step with the declarations.
findings.text: the driving followup `f-awias-001` still reads "§3 follows §2 and the-suite-is-green-at-head §32", while `plan-section-depends-on` (plan.html:24) now declares `s3:[#s2, #s6]`: the cross-plan dependency `the-suite-is-green-at-head#s32` was dropped by the same commit that added §6, and §6 — still `implementable` — is not mentioned. The dropped plan's §32 is done, so nothing is lost by the removal, but the followup now points §3 at an ordering the plan no longer carries

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every path cited in the changed units resolves at the reviewed revision (`reckon/crew/prompts.py` 762 and 840, `reckon/crew/reports.py` 2790/2814, `reckon/crew/promotion_release.py` near 131, `reckon/crew/promotion_records.py` near 126 all exist at the cited content), and `the-suite-is-green-at-head §32` resolves to an existing plan whose §32 is done. The §6 file list resolves as files but misstates their content; that is a claim about the code, reported under reasoning.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §6's third case requires `recovery_watch` and `dispatch_peer` to read an old ledger row's `follow_on_paths`, and neither module contains that symbol; §3's first case has no arm that can fail it (see the reasoning findings).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both changed sections write gates and evidence under `docs/evidence/fragments/additional-work-is-a-section/`, a durable in-repo path, and s6 additionally requires each log to name its revision, the literal command and a trailing `EXIT=`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the changed units name new symbols by mechanism (`outside_scope`, `outside_scope_paths`) and no new symbol, filename or comment carries a stage label, ticket number or version tag.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §6's "key's users" list is drawn from the manifest field, not the ledger key, and §3 names promotion as the caller of a conversion that has no production caller.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s3 carries one deliverable (work outside a worker's fence returns to its coordinator: the field rename, the removal of the followup conversion and the routing of entries to the ledger row are one change), and s6 carries one (the ledger key rename).
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the declared `plan-section-depends-on` for s3 is now `[#s2, #s6]`, but the plan's own driving followup still names the dependency that was dropped and omits §6.
